elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: The only exit in Section 4.1 is the bilateral 90-day notice that prevents the automatic one-year renewal on each anniversary; that is a natural-term non-renewal mechanic (RENEWAL), not a mid-term convenience right. No provision permits the Company to terminate the Agreement or an order at will during the committed one-year term, and the deterministic check 'Customer convenience termination present' returned false.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 requires ninety (90) days' written notice; no 30-day mechanic is proposed and the drafter expressly declined to press the preferred position.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Nothing in Section 4.1 or 4.2 obliges HDI to refund prepaid fees; the only money mechanic runs the other way (Company pays HDI the Termination Payment).

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1's notice right operates only to stop the automatic renewal at an anniversary, so HDI cannot exit for convenience during the one-year committed term. This reading is the same one that defeats preferred element 1.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The quoted words 'unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other' sit inside the auto-renewal sentence and operate as non-renewal at the anniversary, which the rule boundaries direct be assessed under RENEWAL rather than T4C. Section 4.2(a)'s 'In the event the Company terminates' presupposes, but does not grant, an unconditional mid-term convenience right.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Inserted proviso: 'provided that the Termination Payment shall not exceed three (3) months of the fees payable by the Company under Section 3.1.' The cap is unconditional and applies to the whole Net Sales formula, and Section 4.2(c) instalments then run against the capped amount.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: On the non-renewal reading of Section 4.1, HDI's only exit is to stop renewal at an anniversary. Note the residual ambiguity from 'Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated', which on a mid-term reading would let HDI pick any date; the drafter cannot rely on the mid-term reading for element 1 and the end-of-term reading for this element.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 requires 'ninety (90) days written notice to the other' from either Party, so HDI's notice is not shorter than 90 days.

reasons: The fallback level is incomplete: the Customer convenience-termination element is not met. Section 4.1 only lets a Party stop the automatic one-year renewal on 90 days' notice at an anniversary; under the rule boundaries that is non-renewal assessed under RENEWAL, not a termination-for-convenience right, and the deterministic 'Customer convenience termination present' check confirms no such right exists.

The mapping is internally inconsistent: it relies on the same sentence to establish both a Customer convenience right (element 1) and a Vendor right exercisable 'only at the end of a term' (element 3). If the sentence is read as a mid-term convenience right, element 3 fails because HDI would have the same mid-term right; if it is read as end-of-term non-renewal, element 1 fails. Either way the fallback checklist is not complete.

To repair, insert an express operative Customer right, e.g. after the second sentence of Section 4.1: 'Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time, in whole or in part, upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to HDI.' Without that insertion the Section 4.2(a) cap operates on a termination right that the Agreement never grants us.

The cap proviso itself is well drafted and minimal — one clause appended to the existing formula, no deletions, no survival tails, no extra damages or procedure language, and the 'if any' and quarterly instalment mechanics in Section 4.2(c) continue to operate against the capped amount.

Verify before sending that Section 3.1 is in fact the Company's fee-payment provision and that fees are payable by the Company (not HDI); if Section 3.1 does not carry a Company-payable fee stream, the cap resolves to an undefined or nil amount and would become a dangling cross-reference.

Deviation status is correct, but the margin comment overstates the position: it should say we are both capping the Termination Payment and adding the missing Customer convenience right, rather than asserting that Section 4.1 'already lets us exit on ninety days' notice'.
